clause.content: by identifying and evaluating any technologies being developed by the private sector relating to the focus areas described in section 454(c);
by identifying technology gaps in the private sector or other Federal agencies in those focus areas, and making recommendations to address those gaps;
by surveying and analyzing factors that prevent the adoption of emissions reduction technologies by the private sector; and
by recommending technology screening criteria for technology developed under the program to encourage adoption of the technology by the private sector; and

subparagraph.content: develop the strategic plan described in paragraph (2).

subparagraph.heading: Purpose.—
subparagraph.content: The purpose of the strategic plan developed under paragraph (1)(C) is to set forth a plan for achieving the goals of the program established in section 454(b)(1), including for the focus areas described in section 454(c).

subparagraph.heading: Contents.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The strategic plan developed under paragraph (1)(C) shall—

clause.content: specify near-term and long-term qualitative and quantitative objectives relating to each focus area described in section 454(c), including research, development, demonstration, and commercial application objectives;
leverage existing roadmaps relevant to the program in section 454(b)(1) and the focus areas in section 454(c);
specify the anticipated timeframe for achieving the objectives specified under clause (i);
include plans for developing emissions reduction technologies that are globally cost-competitive, including, as applicable, in developing economies;
identify the appropriate role for investment by the Federal Government, in coordination with the private sector, to achieve the objectives specified under clause (i);
identify the public and private costs of achieving the objectives specified under clause (i); and
estimate the economic and employment impact in the United States of achieving those objectives.

paragraph.heading: Frequency.—
paragraph.content: The Committee shall meet not less frequently than 2 times per year, at the call of the Chair.

paragraph.heading: Initial meeting.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 30 days after the date on which the members are appointed under subsection (b), the Committee shall hold its first meeting.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of the Energy Act of 2020, and not less frequently than once every 3 years thereafter, the Committee shall submit to the Secretary a report on the progress of achieving the purposes of the program.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report under paragraph (1) shall include—

subparagraph.content: a description of any technology innovation opportunities identified by the Committee;
a description of any technology gaps identified by the Committee under subsection (d)(1)(B)(ii);
recommendations for improving technology screening criteria and management of the program;
an evaluation of the progress of the program and the research, development, and demonstration activities funded under the program;
any recommended changes to the focus areas of the program described in section 454(c);
a description of the manner in which the Committee has carried out the duties described in subsection (d)(1) and any relevant findings as a result of carrying out those duties;
if necessary, an update to the strategic plan developed by the Committee under subsection (d)(1)(C);
the progress made in achieving the goals set out in that strategic plan;
a review of the management, coordination, and industry utility of the program;
an assessment of the extent to which progress has been made under the program in developing commercial, cost-competitive technologies in each focus area described in section 454(c); and
an assessment of the effectiveness of the program in coordinating efforts within the Department and with other Federal agencies to achieve the purposes of the program.

subsection.heading: Report to Congress.—
subsection.content: Not later than 60 days after receiving a report from the Committee under subsection (f), the Secretary shall submit a copy of that report to the Committees on Appropriations and Science, Space, and Technology of the House of Representatives, the Committees on Appropriations and Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate, and any other relevant Committee of Congress.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Federal Advisory Committee Act.—
subsection.content: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall apply to the Committee.

section.heading: TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM TO IMPLEMENT INDUSTRIAL EMISSIONS REDUCTION.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible entity” means—

subparagraph.content: a State;
a unit of local government;
a territory or possession of the United States;
a relevant State or local office, including an energy office;
a tribal organization (as defined in section 3765 of title 38, United States Code);
an institution of higher education; and
a private entity; and
a trade association or technical society.

paragraph.heading: Emissions reduction.—
paragraph.content: The term “emissions reduction” has the meaning given the term in section 454(a).

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “program” means the program established under subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of the Energy Act of 2020, the Secretary shall establish a program to provide technical assistance to eligible entities to promote the commercial application of emission reduction technologies developed through the program established in section 454(b).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: An eligible entity desiring technical assistance under the program shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require.

paragraph.heading: Application process.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall seek applications for technical assistance under the program on a periodic basis, but not less frequently than once every 12 months.

paragraph.heading: Factors for consideration.—
paragraph.chapeau: In selecting eligible entities for technical assistance under the program, the Secretary shall, to the maximum extent practicable—

subparagraph.chapeau: give priority to—

clause.content: activities carried out with technical assistance under the program that have the greatest potential for achieving emissions reduction in nonpower industrial sectors;

activities carried out in a State in which there are active or inactive industrial facilities that may be used or retrofitted to carry out activities under the focus areas described in section 454(c); and
activities carried out in an economically distressed area (as described in section 301(a) of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3161(a))); and

subparagraph.chapeau: ensure that—

clause.content: there is geographic diversity among the eligible entities selected; and
the activities carried out with technical assistance under the program reflect a majority of the focus areas described in section 454(c).

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Covered project.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “covered project” means a project—

subparagraph.content: that has been recommended in an energy assessment described in paragraph (2)(A) conducted for an eligible entity; and

subparagraph.chapeau: with respect to which the plant site of that eligible entity—

subclause.content: energy efficiency;
material efficiency;
cybersecurity; or
productivity; or
waste production;
greenhouse gas emissions; or
nongreenhouse gas pollution.

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible entity” means a small- or medium-sized manufacturer that has had an energy assessment completed by—

subparagraph.content: an industrial research and assessment center;
a Department of Energy Combined Heat and Power Technical Assistance Partnership jointly with an industrial research and assessment center; or
a third-party assessor that provides an assessment equivalent to an assessment described in subparagraph (A) or (B), as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Energy service provider.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “energy service provider” means—

subparagraph.content: any business providing technology or services to improve the energy efficiency, water efficiency, power factor, or load management of a manufacturing site or other industrial process in an energy-intensive industry (as defined in section 452(a)); and
any utility operating under a utility energy service project.

paragraph.heading: Industrial research and assessment center.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “industrial research and assessment center” means—

subparagraph.content: an institution of higher education-based industrial research and assessment center that is funded by the Secretary under subsection (b); and
an industrial research and assessment center at a trade school, community college, or union training program that is funded by the Secretary under subsection (f).

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “Program” means the program for implementation grants established under subsection (i)(1).

paragraph.heading: Small- or medium-sized manufacturer.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “small- or medium-sized manufacturer” means a manufacturing firm—

subparagraph.content: the gross annual sales of which are less than $100,000,000;
that has fewer than 500 employees at the plant site of the manufacturing firm; and
the annual energy bills of which total more than $100,000 but less than $3,500,000.

subsection.heading: Institution of Higher Education-based Industrial Research and Assessment Centers.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall provide funding to institution of higher education-based industrial research and assessment centers.

paragraph.heading: Purpose.—
paragraph.chapeau: The purpose of each institution of higher education-based industrial research and assessment center shall be—

subparagraph.content: to provide in-depth assessments of small- and medium-sized manufacturer plant sites to evaluate the facilities, services, and manufacturing operations of the plant sites;

subparagraph.chapeau: to identify opportunities for optimizing energy efficiency and environmental performance, including implementation of—

clause.content: smart manufacturing;
energy management systems;
sustainable manufacturing;
information technology advancements for supply chain analysis, logistics, system monitoring, industrial and manufacturing processes, and other purposes; and
waste management systems;

subparagraph.content: to promote applications of emerging concepts and technologies in small- and medium-sized manufacturers (including water and wastewater treatment facilities and federally owned manufacturing facilities);
to promote research and development for the use of alternative energy sources to supply heat, power, and new feedstocks for energy-intensive industries;
to coordinate with appropriate Federal and State research offices;
to provide a clearinghouse for industrial process and energy efficiency technical assistance resources; and
to coordinate with State-accredited technical training centers and community colleges, while ensuring appropriate services to all regions of the United States.

subsection.heading: Coordination.—
subsection.chapeau: To increase the value and capabilities of the industrial research and assessment centers, the centers shall—

paragraph.content: coordinate with Manufacturing Extension Partnership Centers of the National Institute of Standards and Technology;
coordinate with the Federal Energy Management Program and the Building Technologies Office of the Department of Energy to provide building assessment services to manufacturers;

increase partnerships with the National Laboratories of the Department of Energy to leverage the expertise, technologies, and research and development capabilities of the National Laboratories for national industrial and manufacturing needs;

increase partnerships with energy service providers and technology providers to leverage private sector expertise and accelerate deployment of new and existing technologies and processes for energy efficiency, power factor, and load management;
identify opportunities for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and other air emissions; and
promote sustainable manufacturing practices for small- and medium-sized manufacturers.

subsection.heading: Outreach.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall provide funding for—

paragraph.content: outreach activities by the industrial research and assessment centers to inform small- and medium-sized manufacturers of the information, technologies, and services available; and

paragraph.chapeau: coordination activities by each industrial research and assessment center to leverage efforts with—

subparagraph.content: Federal, State, and Tribal efforts;
the efforts of utilities and energy service providers;
the efforts of regional energy efficiency organizations; and
the efforts of other industrial research and assessment centers.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish a Center of Excellence at not more than 5 of the highest-performing industrial research and assessment centers, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Duties.—
paragraph.chapeau: A Center of Excellence shall coordinate with and advise the industrial research and assessment centers located in the region of the Center of Excellence, including—

subparagraph.chapeau: by mentoring new directors and staff of the industrial research and assessment centers with respect to—

clause.content: the availability of resources; and
best practices for carrying out assessments, including through the participation of the staff of the Center of Excellence in assessments carried out by new industrial research and assessment centers;

subparagraph.content: by providing training to staff and students at the industrial research and assessment centers on new technologies, practices, and tools to expand the scope and impact of the assessments carried out by the centers;

by assisting the industrial research and assessment centers with specialized technical opportunities, including by providing a clearinghouse of available expertise and tools to assist the centers and clients of the centers in assessing and implementing those opportunities;

by identifying and coordinating with regional, State, local, Tribal, and utility energy efficiency programs for the purpose of facilitating efforts by industrial research and assessment centers to connect industrial facilities receiving assessments from those centers with regional, State, local, and utility energy efficiency programs that could aid the industrial facilities in implementing any recommendations resulting from the assessments;
by facilitating coordination between the industrial research and assessment centers and other Federal programs described in paragraphs (1) through (3) of subsection (c); and
by coordinating the outreach activities of the industrial research and assessment centers under subsection (d)(1).

paragraph.heading: Funding.—
paragraph.content: For each fiscal year, out of any amounts made available to carry out this section under subsection (j), the Secretary shall use not less than $500,000 to support each Center of Excellence.

subsection.heading: Expansion of Industrial Research and Assessment Centers.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall provide funding to establish additional industrial research and assessment centers at trade schools, community colleges, and union training programs.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subparagraph (B), to the maximum extent practicable, an industrial research and assessment center established under paragraph (1) shall have the same purpose as an institution of higher education-based industrial research center that is funded by the Secretary under subsection (b)(1).

subparagraph.heading: Consideration of capabilities.—
subparagraph.content: In evaluating or establishing the purpose of an industrial research and assessment center established under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall take into consideration the varying capabilities of trade schools, community colleges, and union training programs.

paragraph.heading: Internships.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall pay the Federal share of associated internship programs under which students work with or for industries, manufacturers, and energy service providers to implement the recommendations of industrial research and assessment centers.

paragraph.heading: Apprenticeships.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall pay the Federal share of associated apprenticeship programs under which—

subparagraph.content: students work with or for industries, manufacturers, and energy service providers to implement the recommendations of industrial research and assessment centers; and

employees of facilities that have received an assessment from an industrial research and assessment center work with or for an industrial research and assessment center to gain knowledge on engineering practices and processes to improve productivity and energy savings.

paragraph.heading: Federal share.—
paragraph.content: The Federal share of the cost of carrying out internship programs described in paragraph (1) and apprenticeship programs described in paragraph (2) shall be 50 percent.

subsection.heading: Small Business Loans.—
subsection.content: The Administrator of the Small Business Administration shall, to the maximum extent practicable, expedite consideration of applications from eligible small business concerns for loans under the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 631 et seq.) to implement recommendations developed by the industrial research and assessment centers.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish a program under which the Secretary shall provide grants to eligible entities to implement covered projects.

paragraph.heading: Application.—
paragraph.content: An eligible entity seeking a grant under the Program shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including a demonstration of need for financial assistance to implement the proposed covered project.

paragraph.heading: Priority.—
paragraph.chapeau: In awarding grants under the Program, the Secretary shall give priority to eligible entities that—

subparagraph.content: have had an energy assessment completed by an industrial research and assessment center; and

subparagraph.chapeau: propose to carry out a covered project with a greater potential for—

clause.content: energy efficiency gains; or
greenhouse gas emissions reductions.

subparagraph.heading: Maximum amount.—
subparagraph.content: The amount of a grant provided to an eligible entity under the Program shall not exceed $300,000.

subparagraph.heading: Federal share.—
subparagraph.content: A grant awarded under the Program for a covered project shall be in an amount that is not more than 50 percent of the cost of the covered project.

subparagraph.heading: Supplement.—
subparagraph.content: A grant received by an eligible entity under the Program shall supplement, not supplant, any private or State funds available to the eligible entity to carry out the covered project.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary for the period of fiscal years 2022 through 2026—

paragraph.content: $150,000,000 to carry out subsections (a) through (h); and
$400,000,000 to carry out subsection (i). * * * * * * *

title.heading: ENERGY SAVINGS IN GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC INSTITUTIONS

subtitle.heading: Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grants

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible entity” means—

subparagraph.content: a State;
an eligible unit of local government; and
an Indian tribe.

paragraph.heading: Eligible unit of local government.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible unit of local government” means—

subparagraph.content: an eligible unit of local government-alternative 1; and
an eligible unit of local government-alternative 2.

subparagraph.heading: Eligible unit of local government-alternative 1.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “eligible unit of local government-alternative 1” means—

subclause.content: of at least 35,000; or
that causes the city to be 1 of the 10 highest-populated cities of the State in which the city is located; and
of at least 200,000; or
that causes the county to be 1 of the 10 highest-populated counties of the State in which the county is located.

subparagraph.heading: Eligible unit of local government-alternative 2.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “eligible unit of local government-alternative 2” means—

clause.content: a city with a population of at least 50,000; or
a county with a population of at least 200,000.

paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian tribe” has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 450b).

paragraph.heading: Program.—
paragraph.content: The term “program” means the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant Program established under section 542(a).

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “State” means—

subparagraph.content: a State;
the District of Columbia;
the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; and
any other territory or possession of the United States.

section.heading: ENERGY EFFICIENCY AND CONSERVATION BLOCK GRANT PROGRAM

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a program, to be known as the “Energy Efficiency and Conservation Block Grant Program”, under which the Secretary shall provide grants to eligible entities in accordance with this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.chapeau: The purpose of the program shall be to assist eligible entities in implementing strategies—

paragraph.chapeau: to reduce fossil fuel emissions created as a result of activities within the jurisdictions of eligible entities in a manner that—

subparagraph.content: is environmentally sustainable; and
to the maximum extent practicable, maximizes benefits for local and regional communities;

paragraph.content: to reduce the total energy use of the eligible entities; and

paragraph.chapeau: to improve energy efficiency in—

subparagraph.content: the transportation sector;
the building sector; and
other appropriate sectors.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Of amounts made available to provide grants under this subtitle for each fiscal year, the Secretary shall allocate—

paragraph.content: 34 percent to eligible units of local government—alternative 1, in accordance with subsection (b);
34 percent to eligible units of local government—alternative 2, in accordance with subsection (b);
28 percent to States in accordance with subsection (c);
2 percent to Indian tribes in accordance with subsection (d); and
2 percent for competitive grants under section 546.

subsection.heading: Eligible Units of Local Government.—
subsection.chapeau: Of amounts available for distribution to eligible units of local government under subsection (a)(1) or (2), the Secretary shall provide grants to eligible units of local government under this section based on a formula established by the Secretary according to—

paragraph.content: the populations served by the eligible units of local government, according to the latest available decennial census; and
the daytime populations of the eligible units of local government and other similar factors (such as square footage of commercial, office, and industrial space), as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: States.—
subsection.chapeau: Of amounts available for distribution to States under subsection (a)(2), the Secretary shall provide—

paragraph.content: not less than 1.25 percent to each State; and

paragraph.chapeau: the remainder among the States, based on a formula to be established by the Secretary that takes into account—

subparagraph.content: the population of each State; and
any other criteria that the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Indian Tribes.—
subsection.content: Of amounts available for distribution to Indian tribes under subsection (a)(3), the Secretary shall establish a formula for allocation of the amounts to Indian tribes, taking into account any factors that the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Publication of Allocation Formulas.—
subsection.content: Not later than 90 days before the beginning of each fiscal year for which grants are provided under this subtitle, the Secretary shall publish in the Federal Register the formulas for allocation established under this section.

subsection.heading: State and Local Advisory Committee.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a State and local advisory committee to advise the Secretary regarding administration, implementation, and evaluation of the program.

section.heading: USE OF FUNDS
section.chapeau: An eligible entity may use a grant received under this subtitle to carry out activities to achieve the purposes of the program, including—

paragraph.content: development and implementation of an energy efficiency and conservation strategy under section 545(b);

paragraph.chapeau: retaining technical consultant services to assist the eligible entity in the development of such a strategy, including—

subparagraph.content: formulation of energy efficiency, energy conservation, and energy usage goals;

subparagraph.chapeau: identification of strategies to achieve those goals—

clause.content: through efforts to increase energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption; and
by encouraging behavioral changes among the population served by the eligible entity;

subparagraph.content: development of methods to measure progress in achieving the goals;

subparagraph.chapeau: development and publication of annual reports to the population served by the eligible entity describing—

clause.content: the strategies and goals; and
the progress made in achieving the strategies and goals during the preceding calendar year; and

subparagraph.content: other services to assist in the implementation of the energy efficiency and conservation strategy;

paragraph.content: conducting residential and commercial building energy audits;
establishment of financial incentive programs for energy efficiency improvements;
the provision of grants to nonprofit organizations and governmental agencies for the purpose of performing energy efficiency retrofits;

paragraph.chapeau: development and implementation of energy efficiency and conservation programs for buildings and facilities within the jurisdiction of the eligible entity, including—

subparagraph.content: design and operation of the programs;
identifying the most effective methods for achieving maximum participation and efficiency rates;
public education;
measurement and verification protocols; and
identification of energy efficient technologies;

paragraph.chapeau: development and implementation of programs to conserve energy used in transportation, including—

subparagraph.content: use of flex time by employers;
satellite work centers;
development and promotion of zoning guidelines or requirements that promote energy efficient development;
development of infrastructure, such as bike lanes and pathways and pedestrian walkways;
synchronization of traffic signals; and
other measures that increase energy efficiency and decrease energy consumption;

paragraph.content: development and implementation of building codes and inspection services to promote building energy efficiency;

paragraph.chapeau: application and implementation of energy distribution technologies that significantly increase energy efficiency, including—

subparagraph.content: distributed resources; and
district heating and cooling systems;

paragraph.content: activities to increase participation and efficiency rates for material conservation programs, including source reduction, recycling, and recycled content procurement programs that lead to increases in energy efficiency;
the purchase and implementation of technologies to reduce, capture, and, to the maximum extent practicable, use methane and other greenhouse gases generated by landfills or similar sources;

paragraph.chapeau: replacement of traffic signals and street lighting with energy efficient lighting technologies, including—

subparagraph.content: light emitting diodes; and
any other technology of equal or greater energy efficiency;

paragraph.chapeau: development, implementation, and installation on or in any government building of the eligible entity of onsite renewable energy technology that generates electricity from renewable resources, including—

subparagraph.content: solar energy;
wind energy;
fuel cells; and
biomass;

paragraph.content: programs for financing energy efficiency, renewable energy, and zero-emission transportation (and associated infrastructure), capital investments, projects, and programs, which may include loan programs and performance contracting programs, for leveraging of additional public and private sector funds, and programs that allow rebates, grants, or other incentives for the purchase and installation of energy efficiency, renewable energy, and zero-emission transportation (and associated infrastructure) measures; and

paragraph.chapeau: any other appropriate activity, as determined by the Secretary, in consultation with—

subparagraph.content: the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency;
the Secretary of Transportation; and
the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: To be eligible to receive a grant under the program, each eligible applicant shall submit to the Secretary a written assurance that all laborers and mechanics employed by any contractor or subcontractor of the eligible entity during any construction, alteration, or repair activity funded, in whole or in part, by the grant shall be paid wages at rates not less than the prevailing wages for similar construction activities in the locality, as determined by the Secretary of Labor, in accordance with sections 3141 through 3144, 3146, and 3147 of title 40, United States Code.

paragraph.heading: Secretary of labor.—
paragraph.chapeau: With respect to the labor standards referred to in paragraph (1), the Secretary of Labor shall have the authority and functions described in—

subparagraph.content: Reorganization Plan Numbered 14 of 1950 (5 U.S.C. 903 note); and
section 3145 of title 40, United States Code.

subsection.heading: Eligible Units of Local Government and Indian Tribes.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date on which an eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe receives a grant under this subtitle, the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe shall submit to the Secretary a proposed energy efficiency and conservation strategy in accordance with this paragraph.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The proposed strategy under subparagraph (A) shall include—

clause.content: a description of the goals of the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe, in accordance with the purposes of this subtitle, for increased energy efficiency and conservation in the jurisdiction of the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe; and
a plan for the use of the grant to assist the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe in achieving those goals, in accordance with section 544.

subparagraph.heading: Requirements for eligible units of local government.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In developing the strategy under subparagraph (A), an eligible unit of local government shall—

clause.content: take into account any plans for the use of funds by adjacent eligible units of local governments that receive grants under the program; and

coordinate and share information with the State in which the eligible unit of local government is located regarding activities carried out using the grant to maximize the energy efficiency and conservation benefits under this subtitle.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall approve or disapprove a proposed strategy under paragraph (1) by not later than 120 days after the date of submission of the proposed strategy.

subparagraph.heading: Disapproval.—
subparagraph.chapeau: If the Secretary disapproves a proposed strategy under subparagraph (A)—

clause.content: the Secretary shall provide to the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe the reasons for the disapproval; and
the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe may revise and resubmit the proposed strategy as many times as necessary until the Secretary approves a proposed strategy.

subparagraph.heading: Requirement.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall not provide to an eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe any grant under the program until a proposed strategy of the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe is approved by the Secretary under this paragraph.

paragraph.heading: Limitations on use of funds.—
paragraph.chapeau: Of amounts provided to an eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe under the program, an eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe may use—

subparagraph.chapeau: for administrative expenses, excluding the cost of meeting the reporting requirements of this subtitle, an amount equal to the greater of—

clause.content: 10 percent; and

subparagraph.chapeau: for the establishment of revolving loan funds, an amount equal to the greater of—

clause.content: 20 percent; and

subparagraph.chapeau: for the provision of subgrants to nongovernmental organizations for the purpose of assisting in the implementation of the energy efficiency and conservation strategy of the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe, an amount equal to the greater of—

clause.content: 20 percent; and

paragraph.heading: Annual report.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date on which funds are initially provided to an eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe under the program, and annually thereafter, the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe shall submit to the Secretary a report describing—

subparagraph.content: the status of development and implementation of the energy efficiency and conservation strategy of the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe; and
as practicable, an assessment of energy efficiency gains within the jurisdiction of the eligible unit of local government or Indian tribe.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: A State that receives a grant under the program shall use not less than 60 percent of the amount received to provide subgrants to units of local government in the State that are not eligible units of local government.

subparagraph.heading: Deadline.—
subparagraph.content: The State shall provide the subgrants required under subparagraph (A) by not later than 180 days after the date on which the Secretary approves a proposed energy efficiency and conservation strategy of the State under paragraph (3).

paragraph.heading: Revision of conservation plan; proposed strategy.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, each State shall—

subparagraph.content: modify the State energy conservation plan of the State under section 362 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (42 U.S.C. 6322) to establish additional goals for increased energy efficiency and conservation in the State; and

subparagraph.chapeau: submit to the Secretary a proposed energy efficiency and conservation strategy that—

clause.content: establishes a process for providing subgrants as required under paragraph (1); and
includes a plan of the State for the use of funds received under the program to assist the State in achieving the goals established under subparagraph (A), in accordance with sections 542(b) and 544.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall approve or disapprove a proposed strategy under paragraph (2)(B) by not later than 120 days after the date of submission of the proposed strategy.

subparagraph.heading: Disapproval.—
subparagraph.chapeau: If the Secretary disapproves a proposed strategy under subparagraph (A)—

clause.content: the Secretary shall provide to the State the reasons for the disapproval; and
the State may revise and resubmit the proposed strategy as many times as necessary until the Secretary approves a proposed strategy.

subparagraph.heading: Requirement.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall not provide to a State any grant under the program until a proposed strategy of the State is approved by the Secretary under this paragraph.

paragraph.heading: Limitations on use of funds.—
paragraph.content: A State may use not more than 10 percent of amounts provided under the program for administrative expenses.

paragraph.heading: Annual reports.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each State that receives a grant under the program shall submit to the Secretary an annual report that describes—

subparagraph.content: the status of development and implementation of the energy efficiency and conservation strategy of the State during the preceding calendar year;
the status of the subgrant program of the State under paragraph (1);
the energy efficiency gains achieved through the energy efficiency and conservation strategy of the State during the preceding calendar year; and
specific energy efficiency and conservation goals of the State for subsequent calendar years.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.chapeau: Of the total amount made available for each fiscal year to carry out this subtitle, the Secretary shall use not less than 2 percent to provide grants under this section, on a competitive basis, to—

paragraph.content: units of local government (including Indian tribes) that are not eligible entities; and
consortia of units of local government described in paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Applications.—
subsection.content: To be eligible to receive a grant under this section, a unit of local government or consortia shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including a plan of the unit of local government to carry out an activity described in section 544.

subsection.heading: Priority.—
subsection.chapeau: In providing grants under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to units of local government—

paragraph.content: located in States with populations of less than 2,000,000; or
that plan to carry out projects that would result in significant energy efficiency improvements or reductions in fossil fuel use.

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may review and evaluate the performance of any eligible entity that receives a grant under the program, including by conducting an audit, as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Withholding of Funds.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may withhold from an eligible entity any portion of a grant to be provided to the eligible entity under the program if the Secretary determines that the eligible entity has failed to achieve compliance with—

paragraph.content: any applicable guideline or regulation of the Secretary relating to the program, including the misuse or misappropriation of funds provided under the program; or
the energy efficiency and conservation strategy of the eligible entity.

paragraph.heading: Grants.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary for the provision of grants under the program $2,000,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2012.

paragraph.heading: Administrative costs.—
paragraph.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary for administrative expenses of the program—

subparagraph.content: $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 and 2009;
$25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2010 and 2011; and
$30,000,000 for fiscal year 2012.

subsection.heading: Maintenance of Funding.—
subsection.chapeau: The funding provided under this section shall supplement (and not supplant) other Federal funding provided under—

paragraph.content: a State energy conservation plan established under part D of title III of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (42 U.S.C. 6321 et seq.); or
the Weatherization Assistance Program for Low-Income Persons established under part A of title IV of the Energy Conservation and Production Act (42 U.S.C. 6861 et seq.).

subtitle.heading: Geothermal Energy

section.heading: SHORT TITLE
section.content: This subtitle may be cited as the “Advanced Geothermal Energy Research and Development Act of 2007”.

paragraph.heading: Engineered.—
paragraph.chapeau: When referring to enhanced geothermal systems, the term “engineered” means designed to access subsurface heat, including stimulation and nonstimulation technologies to address one or more of the following issues:

subparagraph.content: Lack of effective permeability, porosity or open fracture connectivity within the heat reservoir.
Insufficient contained geofluid in the heat reservoir.
A low average geothermal gradient which necessitates deeper drilling, or the use of alternative heat sources or heat generation processes.

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible entity” means any of the following entities:

subparagraph.content: An institution of higher education.
A National laboratory.
A Federal research agency.
A State research agency.
A nonprofit research organization.
An industrial entity.
A consortium of 2 or more entities described in subparagraphs (A) through (F).

paragraph.heading: Enhanced geothermal systems.—
paragraph.content: The term “enhanced geothermal systems” means geothermal reservoir systems that are engineered, as opposed to occurring naturally.

paragraph.heading: Geofluid.—
paragraph.content: The term “geofluid” means any fluid used to extract thermal energy from the Earth which is transported to the surface for direct use or electric power generation, except that such term shall not include oil or natural gas.

paragraph.heading: Geopressured resources.—
paragraph.content: The term “geopressured resources” mean geothermal deposits found in sedimentary rocks under higher than normal pressure and saturated with gas or methane.

paragraph.heading: Geothermal.—
paragraph.content: The term “geothermal” refers to heat energy stored in the Earth’s crust that can be accessed for direct use or electric power generation.

paragraph.heading: Hydrothermal.—
paragraph.content: The term “hydrothermal” refers to naturally occurring subsurface reservoirs of hot water or steam.

paragraph.heading: Systems approach.—
paragraph.content: The term “systems approach” means an approach to solving problems or designing systems that attempts to optimize the performance of the overall system, rather than a particular component of the system.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application for geothermal energy production from hydrothermal systems.

subsection.heading: Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: The program authorized in subsection (a) shall include the following:

paragraph.heading: Advanced hydrothermal resource tools.—
paragraph.content: The research and development of advanced geologic tools to assist in locating hydrothermal resources, and to increase the reliability of site characterization, including the development of new imaging and sensing technologies and techniques to assist in prioritization of targets for characterization;

paragraph.heading: Exploratory drilling for geothermal resources.—
paragraph.content: The demonstration of advanced technologies and techniques of siting and exploratory drilling for undiscovered resources in a variety of geologic settings, carried out in collaboration with industry partners that will assist in the acquisition of high quality data sets relevant for hydrothermal subsurface characterization activities.

section.heading: GENERAL GEOTHERMAL SYSTEMS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.

subsection.heading: Subsurface Components and Systems.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall support a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of components and systems capable of withstanding geothermal environments and necessary to develop, produce, and monitor geothermal reservoirs and produce geothermal energy.

subsection.heading: Environmental Impacts.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: support a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of technologies and practices designed to mitigate or preclude potential adverse environmental impacts of geothermal energy development, production or use;

support a research program to identify potential environmental impacts, including induced seismicity, and environmental benefits of geothermal energy development, production, and use, and ensure that the program described in paragraph (1) addresses such impacts, including water use and effects on groundwater and local hydrology;

support a program of research to compare the potential environmental impacts and environmental benefits identified as part of the development, production, and use of geothermal energy with the potential emission reductions of greenhouse gases gained by geothermal energy development, production, and use; and
in carrying out this section, the Secretary shall, to the maximum extent practicable, consult with relevant federal agencies, including the Environmental Protection Agency.

subsection.heading: Reservoir Thermal Energy Storage.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall support a program of research, development, and demonstration of reservoir thermal energy storage, emphasizing cost-effective improvements through deep direct use engineering, design, and systems research.

subsection.heading: Oil and Gas Technology Transfer Initiative.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall support an initiative among the Office of Fossil Energy, the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, and the private sector to research, develop, and demonstrate relevant advanced technologies and operation techniques used in the oil and gas sector for use in geothermal energy development.

paragraph.heading: Priorities.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Secretary shall prioritize technologies with the greatest potential to significantly increase the use and lower the cost of geothermal energy in the United States, including the cost and speed of geothermal drilling surface technologies, large- and small-scale drilling, and well construction.

subsection.heading: Coproduction of Geothermal Energy and Minerals Production Research and Development Initiative.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall carry out a research and development initiative under which the Secretary shall provide financial assistance to demonstrate the coproduction of critical minerals from geothermal resources.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: An award made under paragraph (1) shall—

subparagraph.content: improve the cost effectiveness of removing minerals from geothermal brines as part of the coproduction process;
increase recovery rates of the targeted mineral commodity;
decrease water use and other environmental impacts, as determined by the Secretary; and
demonstrate a path to commercial viability.

subsection.heading: Flexible Operations.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall support a research initiative on flexible operation of geothermal power plants.

subsection.heading: Integrated Energy Systems.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall identify opportunities for joint research, development, and demonstration programs between geothermal systems and other energy generation or storage systems.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior, establish and operate a voluntary, industry-wide repository of geothermal drilling information to lower the cost of future geothermal drilling.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: In carrying out paragraph (1), the Secretary shall collaborate with countries utilizing a significant amount of geothermal energy, as determined by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Data system.—
subparagraph.content: The repository established under paragraph (1) shall be integrated with the National Geothermal Data System.

section.heading: ENHANCED GEOTHERMAL SYSTEMS RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall support a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application for enhanced geothermal systems, including the programs described in subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Enhanced Geothermal Systems Technologies.—
subsection.chapeau: In collaboration with industry partners, institutions of higher education, and the national laboratories, the Secretary shall support a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of the technologies to achieve higher efficiency and lower cost enhanced geothermal systems, including—

paragraph.content: reservoir stimulation;
drilled, non-stimulated (e.g. closed-loop) reservoir technologies;
reservoir characterization, monitoring, and modeling and understanding of the surface area and volume of fractures;
stress and fracture mapping including real time monitoring and modeling;
tracer development;
three and four-dimensional seismic imaging and tomography;
well placement and orientation;
long-term reservoir management;
drilling technologies, methods, and tools;
improved exploration tools;
zonal isolation; and
understanding induced seismicity risks from reservoir engineering and stimulation.

subsection.heading: Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall support the establishment and construction of up to 3 field research sites, which shall each be known as a “Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy” or “FORGE” site to develop, test, and enhance techniques and tools for enhanced geothermal energy.

paragraph.heading: Duties.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: provide financial assistance in support of research and development projects focused on advanced monitoring technologies, new technologies and approaches for implementing multi-zone stimulations, nonstimulation techniques, and dynamic reservoir modeling that incorporates all available high-fidelity characterization data; and

seek opportunities to coordinate efforts and share information with domestic and international partners engaged in research and development of geothermal systems and related technology, including coordination between FORGE sites.

paragraph.heading: Site selection.—
paragraph.chapeau: Of the FORGE sites referred to in paragraph (1), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: consider applications through a competitive, merit-reviewed process, from National Laboratories, multi-institutional collaborations, institutes of higher education and other appropriate entities best suited to provide national leadership on geothermal related issues and perform the duties enumerated under this subsection;
prioritize existing field sites and facilities with capabilities relevant to the duties enumerated under this subsection;
determine the mission need for and potential location of subsequent FORGE sites following the completion of construction and one year of operation of two FORGE sites; and
ensure geologic diversity among FORGE sites when developing subsequent sites, to the maximum extent practicable.

paragraph.heading: Existing forge sites.—
paragraph.content: A FORGE site already in existence on the date of enactment of this Act may continue to receive support.

subparagraph.heading: Initial duration.—
subparagraph.content: FORGE sites selected under paragraph (3) shall operate for an initial term of not more than 7 years after the date on which site operation begins.

subparagraph.heading: Performance metrics.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall establish performance metrics for each FORGE site supported under this paragraph, which may be used by the Secretary to determine whether a FORGE site should continue to receive funding.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: At the end of an operational term described in subparagraph (B), a FORGE site may—

clause.content: be transferred to other public or private entities for further enhanced geothermal testing; or
subject to appropriations and a merit review by the Secretary, operate for an additional term of not more than 7 years.

subparagraph.heading: Operational term described.—
subparagraph.chapeau: An operational term referred to in subparagraph (A)—

clause.content: in the case of an existing FORGE site, is the existing operational term; and
in the case of new FORGE sites selected under paragraph (3), is the initial term under paragraph (5)(A) or an additional term under subparagraph (A)(ii) of this paragraph.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Out of funds authorized to be appropriated under section 623, there shall be made available to the Secretary to carry out the FORGE activities under this paragraph—

clause.content: $45,000,000 for fiscal year 2021;
$55,000,000 for fiscal year 2022;
$65,000,000 for fiscal year 2023;
$70,000,000 for fiscal year 2024; and
$70,000,000 for fiscal year 2025.

subparagraph.heading: Considerations.—
subparagraph.content: In carrying out this subsection, the Secretary shall consider the balance between funds dedicated to construction and operations and research activities to reflect the state of site development.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Beginning on the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary, in collaboration with industry partners, institutions of higher education, and the national laboratories, shall support an initiative for demonstration of enhanced geothermal systems for power production or direct use.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Under the initiative described in paragraph (1), 4 demonstration projects shall be carried out in locations that are potentially commercially viable for enhanced geothermal systems development, while also considering environmental impacts to the maximum extent practicable, as determined by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Requirements.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Demonstration projects under subparagraph (A) shall—

subclause.content: different geologic settings, such as hot sedimentary aquifers, layered geologic systems, supercritical systems, and basement rock systems; and
a variety of development techniques, including open hole and cased hole completions, differing well orientations, and stimulation and nonstimulation mechanisms; and

clause.content: to the extent practicable, use existing sites where subsurface characterization or geothermal energy integration analysis has been conducted.

subparagraph.heading: Eastern demonstration.—
subparagraph.content: Not fewer than 1 of the demonstration projects carried out under subparagraph (A) shall be located an area east of the Mississippi River that is suitable for enhanced geothermal demonstration for power, heat, or a combination of power and heat.

subparagraph.heading: Milestone-based demonstration projects.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may carry out demonstration projects under this subsection as a milestone-based demonstration project under section 9005 of the Energy Act of 2020.

paragraph.heading: Funding.—
paragraph.content: Out of funds authorized to be appropriated under section 623, there shall be made available to the Secretary to carry out the demonstration activities under this subsection $21,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2021 through 2025.

section.heading: GEOTHERMAL ENERGY PRODUCTION FROM OIL AND GAS FIELDS AND RECOVERY AND PRODUCTION OF GEOPRESSURED GAS RESOURCES

subsection.heading: In general.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application to support development of geothermal energy production from oil and gas fields and production and recovery of energy, including electricity, from geopressured resources. In addition, the Secretary shall conduct such supporting activities including research, resource characterization, and technology development as necessary.

subsection.heading: Geothermal Energy Production From Oil and Gas Fields.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall implement a grant program in support of geothermal energy production from oil and gas fields. The program shall include grants for a total of not less than three demonstration projects of the use of geothermal techniques such as advanced organic rankine cycle systems at marginal, unproductive, and productive oil and gas wells. The Secretary shall, to the extent practicable and in the public interest, make awards that—

paragraph.content: include not less than five oil or gas well sites per project award;
use a range of oil or gas well hot water source temperatures from 150 degrees Fahrenheit to 300 degrees Fahrenheit;
cover a range of sizes up to one megawatt;
are located at a range of sites;
can be replicated at a wide range of sites;
facilitate identification of optimum techniques among competing alternatives;
include business commercialization plans that have the potential for production of equipment at high volumes and operation and support at a large number of sites; and
satisfy other criteria that the Secretary determines are necessary to carry out the program and collect necessary data and information.

subsection.continuation: The Secretary shall give preference to assessments that address multiple elements contained in paragraphs (1) through (8).

subsection.heading: Grant Awards.—
subsection.chapeau: Each grant award for demonstration of geothermal technology such as advanced organic rankine cycle systems at oil and gas wells made by the Secretary under subsection (b) shall include—

paragraph.content: necessary and appropriate site engineering study;
detailed economic assessment of site specific conditions;
appropriate feasibility studies to determine whether the demonstration can be replicated;
design or adaptation of existing technology for site specific circumstances or conditions;
installation of equipment, service, and support;
operation for a minimum of 1 year and monitoring for the duration of the demonstration; and
validation of technical and economic assumptions and documentation of lessons learned.

subsection.heading: Geopressured Gas Resource Recovery and Production.—

paragraph.content: The Secretary shall implement a program to support the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of cost-effective techniques to produce energy from geopressured resources.
The Secretary shall solicit preliminary engineering designs for geopressured resources production and recovery facilities.

Based upon a review of the preliminary designs, the Secretary shall award grants, which may be cost-shared, to support the detailed development and completion of engineering, architectural and technical plans needed to support construction of new designs.

Based upon a review of the final design plans above, the Secretary shall award cost-shared development and construction grants for demonstration geopressured production facilities that show potential for economic recovery of the heat, kinetic energy and gas resources from geopressured resources.

subsection.heading: Competitive Grant Selection.—
subsection.content: Not less than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall conduct a national solicitation for applications for grants under the programs outlined in subsections (b) and (d). Grant recipients shall be selected on a competitive basis based on criteria in the respective subsection.

subsection.heading: Well Drilling.—
subsection.content: No funds may be used under this section for the purpose of drilling new wells.

section.heading: GEOTHERMAL HEAT PUMPS AND DIRECT USE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.

subsection.heading: Purposes.—
subsection.chapeau: The purposes of this section are—

paragraph.content: to improve the understanding of related earth sciences, components, processes, and systems used for geothermal heat pumps and the direct use of geothermal energy; and
to increase the energy efficiency, lower the cost, increase the use, and improve and demonstrate the effectiveness of geothermal heat pumps and the direct use of geothermal energy.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Direct use of geothermal energy.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “direct use of geothermal energy” means geothermal systems that use water directly or through a heat exchanger to provide—

subparagraph.content: heating and cooling to buildings, commercial districts, residential communities, and large municipal, or industrial projects; or
heat required for industrial processes, agriculture, aquaculture, and other facilities.

paragraph.heading: Economically distressed area.—
paragraph.content: The term “economically distressed area” means an area described in section 301(a) of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3161(a)).

paragraph.heading: Geothermal heat pump.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “geothermal heat pump” means a system that provides heating and cooling by exchanging heat from shallow geology, groundwater, or surface water using—

subparagraph.content: a closed loop system, which transfers heat by way of buried or immersed pipes that contain a mix of water and working fluid; or
an open loop system, which circulates ground or surface water directly into the building and returns the water to the same aquifer or surface water source.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall support within the Geothermal Technologies Office a program of research, development, and demonstration for geothermal heat pumps and the direct use of geothermal energy.

paragraph.heading: Areas.—
paragraph.chapeau: The program under paragraph (1) may include research, development, demonstration, and commercial application of—

subparagraph.content: geothermal ground loop efficiency improvements, cost reductions, and improved installation and operations methods;
the use of geothermal energy for building-scale energy storage;
the use of geothermal energy as a grid management resource or seasonal energy storage;
geothermal heat pump efficiency improvements;
the use of alternative fluids as a heat exchange medium, such as hot water found in mines and mine shafts, graywater, or other fluids that may improve the economics of geothermal heat pumps;
heating of districts, neighborhoods, communities, large commercial or public buildings, and industrial and manufacturing facilities;
the use of low temperature groundwater for direct use; and
system integration of direct use with geothermal electricity production.

paragraph.heading: Environmental impacts.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out the program, the Secretary shall identify and mitigate potential environmental impacts in accordance with section 614(b).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall carry out the program established in subsection (c) by making financial assistance available to State, local, and Tribal governments, institutions of higher education, nonprofit entities, National Laboratories, utilities, and for-profit companies.

paragraph.heading: Priority.—
paragraph.content: In providing financial assistance under this subsection, the Secretary may give priority to proposals that apply to large buildings, commercial districts, and residential communities that are located in economically distressed areas and areas that the Secretary determines to have high economic potential for geothermal district heating based on the report, “Geovision: Harnessing the Heat Beneath our Feet” published by the Department in 2019, or a successor report.

subsection.heading: Federal Share.—
subsection.content: The Federal share of costs of projects funded under this subtitle shall be in accordance with section 988 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005.

subsection.heading: Organization and Administration of Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: Programs under this subtitle shall incorporate the following elements:

paragraph.content: The Secretary shall coordinate with, and where appropriate may provide funds in furtherance of the purposes of this subtitle to, other Department of Energy research and development programs focused on drilling, subsurface characterization, and other related technologies.
The Secretary shall coordinate and consult with the appropriate Federal land management agencies in selecting proposals for funding under this subtitle.
Nothing in this subtitle shall be construed to alter or affect any law relating to the management or protection of Federal lands.

subsection.heading: Education and Outreach.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the activities described in this subtitle, the Secretary shall support education and outreach activities to disseminate information on geothermal energy technologies and the geothermal energy workforce, including activities at the Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy site or sites.

subsection.heading: Technical Assistance.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this subtitle, the Secretary shall also conduct technical assistance and analysis activities with eligible entities for the purpose of supporting the commercial application of advances in geothermal energy systems development and operations, which may include activities that support expanding access to advanced geothermal energy technologies for rural, Tribal, and low-income communities.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Every 5 years after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Secretary shall report to the Committee on Science and Technology of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate on advanced concepts and technologies to maximize the geothermal resource potential of the United States.

subsection.heading: Progress Reports.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this subsection, and every 2 years thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Science and Technology of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate a report on the results of projects undertaken under this part and other such information the Secretary considers appropriate.

section.heading: ADVANCED GEOTHERMAL COMPUTING AND DATA SCIENCE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out a program of research and development of advanced computing and data science tools for geothermal energy.

subsection.heading: Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: The program authorized in subsection (a) shall include the following:

paragraph.heading: Advanced computing for geothermal systems technologies.—
paragraph.content: Research, development, and demonstration of technologies to develop advanced data, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and related computing tools to assist in locating geothermal resources, to increase the reliability of site characterization, to increase the rate and efficiency of drilling, to improve induced seismicity mitigation, and to support enhanced geothermal systems technologies.

paragraph.heading: Geothermal systems reservoir modeling.—
paragraph.content: Research, development, and demonstration of models of geothermal reservoir performance and enhanced geothermal systems reservoir stimulation technologies and techniques, with an emphasis on accurately modeling fluid and heat flow, permeability evolution, geomechanics, geochemistry, seismicity, and operational performance over time, including collaboration with industry and field validation.

subsection.heading: Coordination.—
subsection.content: In carrying out these programs, the Secretary shall ensure coordination and consultation with the Department of Energy’s Office of Science. The Secretary shall ensure, to the maximum extent practicable, coordination of these activities with the Department of Energy National Laboratories, institutes of higher education, and the private sector.

section.heading: GEOTHERMAL WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT.
section.chapeau: The Secretary shall support the development of a geothermal energy workforce through a program that—

paragraph.content: facilitates collaboration between university students and researchers at the National Laboratories; and
prioritizes science in areas relevant to the mission of the Department through the application of geothermal energy tools and technologies.
